chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: How Tate avoided the draft
summary: A friend on the draft board kept postponing his induction until he was classified 4-F.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: They didn't want me. I had a friend.
You know, maybe -- I don't know. You think I should say --
Sure. It goes into their archives and it's -- it isn't something that anyone's going to be publishing.

Yeah. Well, look, I had a Jewish friend that was up to -- my draft center was right around 146th Street, see? And there was a box actually about as long as from here to over there. And he used to tell me all the time, he said, "You know, it would be a shame for them to put you in the Army," he says, "because I know you don't want to go and you're doind a lot of nice things here by playing with the band. You're playing Army things and so on," he says, "but I'm going to try to see -- I'm going to try to look out after you." He says, "But whenever you come up here, don't go in front of those blacks. Man," he says, "I don't understand why they so hard on each other." He told me that. When I -- man, if I'd see one, if I was going to be next, I'd go to the bathroom and come back so I could go under, you know, somebody else, a white or him, you know. So he used to just keep putting it back, keep putting it back, keep putting it back.
So I don't want to get anybody in trouble, you know. I don't know where he is now, really. But I was like 2-F. When
I got on to -- I never did get on to 1-A. I guess I did, I got to 1-A. 1-A is when they might call you anytime.

So there were four brothers uptown. He told me to find one that they -- you know, when we was going like -- they would examine you uptown, then they'd send you on downtown center, on down to -- so there was four lines, Gary, and you wouldn't believe this -- I don't know one brother from another one. Do you know I got in the right line and I wasn't going to get in the line because it was freezing that day and everybody's standing out in the cold, you know, and when they get up, I could see his name there, you know. So I says, "Are you so and so?" He says, "Yeah." I say, "I'm Buddy Tate." He said, "Oh, yeah, go right in that room, right in there." Carried me right in that room. So I went in and he says, "Nick told me what to do for you," he says, "you're with my favorite band, you know."

I swear to God. He says, "Don't worry about it." So he fixed me up and I kept -- you know, I kept getting suspensions -- you know, like they kept putting it back -- so finally, when he got to 4-F, I knew I wasn't going, see? So I didn't go. So --
